FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 22 November 1977, after the draft finalized by the Organic Chemicals ( Miscellaneous ) Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 Trimethylamine is used in the manufacture of epoxy resins, animal feeds, drugs and pharmaceuticals, ion-exchange resins, agricultural chemicals, etc. It also finds use in germicides, textiles, detergents and It is corrosion inhibitors, and as catalyst for reaction polymerization. also widely used as plant growth controller and solvent. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in The number of significant places retainaccordance with IS : 2-1960*. ed in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

T&e IS1 Mark on prodbcts covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity fo that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certil%ation Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

A-2.3.2 Determination of Response Factors - Check and adjust the chromatograph. Inject 1 ~1 of the standard mixture with the help of the hypodermic syringe. By suitably manipulating, the attenuator switch, record all the peaks on the chart. Measure the area of all the individual peaks. Calculate the response factors as follows: a) Corresponding to each peak of the standard mixture, determine j the amount of area produced by mass percent of the component. b) Select one peak ( monomethylamine ) as a reference. Set its response factor ( area by mass percent ) equal to 1 and express all other response factors relative to it. the sample A-2.3.3 Sample Injection - Connect the bomb containing under pressure vertically to one end of the heated coil in the oven with Connect the other end ( exit end ) of the swage lock metallic fittings. coil with rubber tubing to a bubbler, half-filled with water, the exit end of the bubbler being connected to a long rubber tubing which is taken outside the room as a vent. Now open slowly the bottom valve of the sample bomb. The sample would get immediately vaporized as it passes through the heated coil kept at 150�C. Take the vapour coming out through the outlet end of the coil in the 2-ml syringe by piercing the needle through the connecting rubber tubing. Inject 1 ml of the gaseous sample into the chromatograph and, by suitably manipulating the attenuator, record all the peaks on the chart. Measure the areas of all the peaks and calculate ( m/m ) of each component as in A-2.4. 7 the percentage

A-3.0 General - The strength of a particular methylamine in solution In the first stage, total alkalinity of the is determined in two stages. solution is determined by titrating against standard acid and the In the alkalinity expressed in terms of percent of the particular amine. second stage, the impurities in the solution are determined gas chromatographically and each impurity ( ammonia and amines ) is expressed as The sum total the corresponding amine of which the solution is made. of these impurities is then subtracted from the total amine content to get the percent of the trimethylamine. samples from a tank or drum should be drawn of filling. In that case equal amounts of the operation material shall be collected at regular intervals so as to get a total of Where it is not possible to take a sample during filling, about 1500 ml. the material shall be drawn from different positions and depths with the sampling bottle or can after thoroughly agitating the material so as to ensure a fair amount of homogeneity.
